'''Squeerie''' was a [[Squib/Legends|Squib]] scavenger who operated on the planet [[Almas]] under an exclusive contract from [[Klis Joo]], a former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the mayor of [[Forard]]. He led a salvage team made up of fellow Squibs and a [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] named [[Korq]].

==History==
Squeerie was either born on [[Almas]] or immigrated there. After the former Jedi [[Klis Joo]] became the mayor of [[Forard]], Squeerie negotiated a contract to operate the only licensed salvage company on the world. He formed a team of fellow [[Squib/Legends|Squibs]] and hired a [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] named [[Korq]] for his ability to tear apart found components.<ref name="DC 7" />

Around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], Squeerie and his crew found a crashed airspeeder and started salvage operations. There was a body in the wreckage, so the team respectfully covered it with a tarp. Still, salvage was salvage, and Squeerie and his mates got to work.<ref name="DC 7" />

They were approached by a team working for [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Lanius Qel-Bertuk]], to find some missing Jedi. Fearing unlicensed competitors, Squeerie tried to shoo them away, but the strangers bartered with the Squib for a chance to view the wreckage. There, they identified the body as that of a [[Human/Legends|human]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] named [[Alkin Saad]]. They also determined that the speeder crashed due to an explosion in its repulsor engine.<ref name="DC 7" />

Squeerie and his crew soon found themselves beset by another outsider, a crazed [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] whom the other strangers seemed to recognize. The salvagers stepped aside while the outsiders dealt with one another;<ref name="DC 7" /> eventually the agents subdued the Duros, who turned out to be a Jedi named [[Tantron Dow]], master of the fallen Padawan.<ref name="Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries">{{LivingForce|Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries}}</ref> Squeerie was dismayed to learn that the Jedi was the owner of the crashed speeder, which negated his right to salvage the wreck. The Duros explained that the damage to his airspeeder came from someone firing on him with a cannon.<ref name="DC 8">{{LivingForce|Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries}}</ref> Squeerie paid the agents some credits to thank them for saving him from the crazed Jedi.<ref name="DC 12">{{LivingForce|Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries}}</ref> Then the Duros set them on their way and negotiated passage back to the [[Almas Academy]] in Forad. Squeerie was just happy to make some profit from the situation.<ref name="DC 8" />

Some years later, Almas Academy was destroyed by [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]] during [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]. Squeerie still held his license two years after the attack,<ref name="Echoes of the Jedi">{{DoD|Echoes of the Jedi}}</ref> and thus had the right to salvage the academy ruins. At one point, he sent a team there under the command of a Squib named [[Jiminaldo-mabbramsti]] (Jimi). The team encountered resistance from a rival group of [[Ugor/Legends|Ugor]] salvagers, but agents of Jedi Master [[Denia]] intervened.<ref name="EOTJ 7-8">{{DoD|Echoes of the Jedi}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Squeerie was a typical member of his species and adhered to standard Squib haggling procedures. He had little command of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], so it was often hard to determine the meaning behind what he was saying.<ref name="DC 7" />

He abided by the law and insisted on the legitimacy of his operations, and he eschewed violence. Even his Trandoshan associate Korq was around for his brute strength at dismantling things rather than as a bruiser.<ref name="DC 7" /> Nevertheless, Squeerie and his team kept blasters at hand in case they needed to stun any aggressors.<ref name="DC 8" /> His teams sometimes met resistance from unlicensed rivals, such as [[Ugor/Legends|Ugors]], so such weapons were occasionally called for.<ref name="EOTJ 7-8" />

He used an [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]] to move about Almas and quickly reach salvage sites.<ref name="DC 7" /> Squeerie kept a datapad and his salvage license on him when he was at a recovery site.<ref name="DC 16">{{LivingForce|Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Squeerie appears in ''[[Almas, Sweet Almas: Desert Cries|Desert Cries]]'', an adventure in the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign for ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|The Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]]. The Squib is part of an encounter wherein the player characters meet the missing Jedi Tantron Dow. The characters must get past Squeerie to see the wreckage he is salvaging, which holds clues to advance their quest.<ref name="DC 7" />

According to the adventure's notes to gamemasters, Jedi characters can try to mind trick Squeerie, but making him give up his salvage (which is legally his) is a potentially evil action that moves the Jedi further toward the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], at the gamemaster's discretion. Physically assaulting Squeerie and his crew also counts as an evil action. This article assumes that players take the course of action that gives the best results for them.<ref name="DC 7" />

The amount of money Squeerie pays the player characters depends on their character level and the difficulty of the adventure, ranging from 500 credits per character to 1,500 credits per character.<ref name="DC 12" />

Squeerie's associate, Jiminaldo-mabbramsti, appears in a later RPG adventure, ''[[Echoes of the Jedi]]'', but Squeerie himself makes no appearance.<ref name="EOTJ 7-8" />
